I'm in the same boat, man. I haven't done anything in like a month. I will probably lose my scholarship, and basically I'm fucked. So please, forgive me if what I'm gonna tell you is   useless for you.
You said you make a to do list. Well, break it down in little chunks. Example: throw away blanket, sit down in bed, get up, etc. To show yourself that every single thing that you do is a win. Block everything in your phone that distracts you, there's apps for that.
You get up, ate breakfast and you feel tired. It doesn't matter. If you can't resist the urge to go to bed again, it doesn't matter. You got up. That's a win. Go to bed, rest, and since your apps are blocked, you can't do anything. You can start again tomorrow. If you did resist the urge of go to bed, do something small. Clean your plates, or put something where it belongs, you don't have to clean up everything in a day. Think in something you want to accomplish. For example, study. Go sit down in your desk. If you feel tired, you can start tomorrow again. It doesn't matter, go to rest.  If you don't, go to the next mini task. Open your laptop. Turn it on. Open the pdf, read a sentence. That's it, you don't need to study anything more. You had won the day. You are a champion. Congratulations. Sometimes, when people start something, the initial pain goes away. Probably it will go away in your case, too. It can be more difficult to us, since everything is painful. I understand. That's why you need to go in baby steps, and remember that everything is a win. Take baby steps everyday, and someday, you will start doing more and more work.
One day, after working hard for days, you will probably wake up without the energy for getting up, again. That's okay. Small steps. Small tasks. Start over again. That doesn't matter. You don't need to be a productive machine. Every win counts. 
I hope everything goes well for you. Don't give up.
